entries.subject: LROC WAC global morphologic mosaic v1.3
entries.finding: Selected 643 nm morphology product supplies Monochrome, with original shadows and gaps retained.

entries.subject: LRO LOLA LDEM16 v3.1
entries.finding: Selected grid supplies Elevation above the stated reference sphere; spacing and quantization are not terrain accuracy.

entries.subject: LRO Diviner GHRM v1.0 thermal products
entries.finding: Three selected products supply Midnight temperature, heat anomaly and rock abundance with polar and internal gaps retained.

entries.subject: USGS Unified Geologic Map v2
entries.finding: Selected 49-unit map supplies categorical Geology, not observed color.

entries.subject: Lucey et al. 2021 Christiansen-feature raster
entries.finding: Selected wavelength map supplies the silicate-signature lens; it is not mineral abundance.

entries.subject: NASA Moon Kit and LROC Hapke color alternatives
entries.finding: The documented survey found filled CGI polar coverage and color tiles limited to 70 degrees with less relief than the selected morphology product.
entries.revisitWhen: A registered color product retains polar coverage and comparable source detail.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Hapke model of Sato et al. (2014) at 643 nm, the model the WAC global morphologic mosaic was corrected with: form, fixed values and fitted limits (incidence below 75, emission below 30, phase below 97 degrees) from the paper; w 0.3854, b 0.2375 and h_S 0.0672 are medians of the PDS 643 nm parameter map from 30S to 30N, because the paper prints no global w; c and B_S0 follow from the paper's eq. 2 and 4. Relative to the flood-lit disc centre and held at 30 degrees emission toward the limb.

entries.subject: Shared sphere bank lighting (Lambert with a 0.35 flood floor and 0.05 ambient term, adapted from OpenSpace)
entries.finding: Replaced by the published Hapke law of Sato et al. (2014); the Moon now bakes its own bank.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Native numeric USGS products and compact display grids
entries.finding: Eight 2016 Kaguya MI views plus a shared companion-fit coverage gate; FeO outside 0–100 weight percent is masked. Native samples and all compact-cell calibration and masks are checked. The evidence records the tested file hashes.

entries.subject: GRAIL GRGM1200A gravity anomaly and Bouguer disturbance maps, degree 660
entries.finding: Two numeric views, Gravity (free-air anomaly) and Bouguer gravity (2,500 kg/m3 Bouguer disturbance), in mGal from the PDS RSDMAP products read through their EXTRAS GeoTIFF copies, which match the IMG values cell for cell. Degree 660 is the archived sum just above the label's degree-600 prior limit; its 8.3 km half-wavelength spans about three texels of the 4,096-pixel texture. The evidence records the tested file hashes.

entries.subject: GRGM1200A maps summed to degree 900 and 1200
entries.finding: Not used: the label says a Kaula power-law prior constrains every term above degree 600, so these maps add increasingly prior-shaped detail. Degree 660 already resolves on the largest numeric texture. The evidence records the tested file hashes.
entries.revisitWhen: A release constrains terms above degree 600 with data rather than the Kaula prior.

entries.subject: JPL GL1500E gravity field (Konopliv et al. 2014 lineage)
entries.finding: Not used: the archive holds only its spherical-harmonic coefficients (jggrx_1500e_sha.tab), with no gridded maps or updated covariance; a map would have to be summed here, while GRGM1200A ships archived maps and error maps. The evidence records the tested file hashes.
entries.revisitWhen: The PDS archives gridded GL1500E maps with their error maps.

entries.subject: NASA Moon Trek GRAIL LGRS gravity layers
entries.finding: Not used: Trek serves display tiles of the same GSFC products (for example gggrx_1200a_anom_l660.eq); the views read the numeric PDS originals instead. Trek's crust-mantle interface, crustal-thickness and grain-density layers were not examined here; Crust keeps its existing source. The evidence records the tested file hashes.
entries.revisitWhen: A lens needs a Trek layer whose numeric original the PDS does not archive.

entries.subject: Lunar Prospector GRS elemental abundances (Prettyman et al. 2006), PDS LP-L-GRS-5-ELEM-ABUNDANCE-V1.0, 2 degree equal-area table
entries.finding: Four views in one Surface elements group: Th and K in ppm, FeO and TiO2 in weight percent, from LPGRS_HIGH1_ELEM_ABUNDANCE_2DEG. The data set says these four were the ones evaluated at 2 degrees; the other oxides are advised against there. The table is equal-area, not a grid, so it needs a new shared reader (drafted, not yet in packages). Every pixel matches an independent whitespace decode at its centre and corners. Checked on working changes above ccbf483de8.

entries.subject: The same release's 5 and 20 degree tables
entries.finding: Not used: the 2 degree table carries the same analysis on finer pixels, and the data set names FeO, TiO2, K and Th at 2 degrees as evaluated by Prettyman et al. (2006). The 5 degree table matches the instrument's 5 degree resolution and is less noisy per pixel.
entries.revisitWhen: A view needs MgO, Al2O3, SiO2 or CaO, which the data set advises using at 5 or 20 degrees only.

entries.subject: Lunar Prospector reduced special products (0.5, 2 and 5 degree Th, K, Fe, Ti, H binaries, 2000-2002)
entries.finding: Not used: the page says they are not a PDS peer-reviewed archive; the binaries have no PDS labels; the 2002 elemental maps were superseded by Prettyman et al. (2006), whose abstract says the new cross sections improve on results previously submitted to PDS.
entries.revisitWhen: A peer-reviewed PDS release of the half-degree Th or FeO maps (Lawrence et al. 2002-2003) appears.

entries.subject: Lunar Prospector Neutron Spectrometer hydrogen abundance
entries.finding: The best product is Lawrence et al. (2022): a global 0.5 degree map calibrated to Apollo samples and corrected for rare-earth absorption, archived as 'Global Hydrogen Abundances on the Moon' (CC BY 4.0, doi:10.48732/grc2-4b57, JHU Research Data Repository, v1.0, available 2026-06-02). Its landing page and API answered this machine with a Cloudflare block, so no file was fetched; the block was not bypassed. PDS holds no derived LP hydrogen map: LP-L-NS-3-RDR-V1.0 is time-series count rates. The 2001-2002 special-product hydrogen maps use the model-only calibration of Feldman et al. (2001), are unreviewed and unlabelled, and the page warns they are unreliable where Th and rare earths are high. Lawrence et al. (2022) put their recalibrated maxima about 25% below Lawrence et al. (2006). No archived copy of the 2006 maps was found at the PDS Geosciences Node.
entries.revisitWhen: The doi:10.48732/grc2-4b57 files are downloaded by hand into source/science/lp-ns/ (or the repository allows scripted download), or PDS archives an LP hydrogen map.

entries.subject: LRO LOLA altimetric roughness LDRM_32_50 (2019, 25 m baseline) with its LDRC_32 counts
entries.finding: Tried first and read correctly by the pds3-grid reader with the LDRC_32 count mask (331,175 probes matched an independent decode). The producer filled pixels without shots by interpolation; withholding them removes 37.3% of the area, and at the display textures (about 11 texels per degree, against 32 native pixels per degree) the withheld pixels showed as speckle across the whole globe. Replaced by LDRM_16.
entries.revisitWhen: The Moon's numeric lenses get texture levels finer than about 11 texels per degree, near the product's 32 pixels per degree, so withheld pixels stop reading as speckle.

entries.subject: LRO LOLA surface roughness LDRM_16 V2.0
entries.finding: Roughness view: per-pixel mean of the residual standard deviation of altitudes from three successive shots after a plane fit, 30 to 120 m baseline, 16 pixels/degree, 2009-07-13 to 2011-12-11 (the label cites Zuber et al. 2012). Read by the existing pds3-grid reader; its MISSING_CONSTANT -32768 (4.4% of the area) is withheld, nothing is filled. Checked on working changes above ccbf483de8.

entries.subject: Other LOLA roughness and slope grids: LDRM_32_N (mean), LDRM_32_25 and _75 quantiles, and the LDSM_16 slope map
entries.finding: Not used: the 32 pixel/degree family shares LDRM_32_50's interpolated pixels (see lola-ldrm-32-50). Slope is a different quantity.
entries.revisitWhen: The lola-ldrm-32-50 condition is met and a view needs boulder-sensitive roughness (the 0.75 quantile or mean), or a view needs slope.

entries.subject: LRO Diviner Global Cumulative Products (LRO-L-DLRE-5-GCP-V1.0, Williams et al. 2017) for noon and maximum bolometric temperature
entries.finding: The only archived global daytime product. GHRM, which feeds Midnight temperature, holds night-time fits only, and the Level 3 GDR maps hold rock abundance, soil temperature and the Christiansen feature. GCP is eighteen 156 MB ASCII tables of bin-average temperatures per 0.5 degree cell and 0.25 hour of local time, 2009-07-05 to 2015-04-01, with -9999 for empty bins. No archived bin is centred on noon. A drafted converter keeps archived bin averages only: maximum = the warmest bin of each cell; noon = the 11:45-12:00 or 12:00-12:15 bin, or their mean when both hold data. Tried on the 10S-0 strip: maximum covers every cell, 5th to 95th percentile 387.4-395.2 K, matching Williams et al. (2017), 'about 387-397 K at the equator'; the most common hour of the maximum is 12:00-12:15. Requiring both noon bins leaves 33% of that strip covered, one of them 87%. The PDS Geosciences Node served 0.1-0.5 MB/s, so the other 17 strips (2.6 GB) were not all fetched in this session and the lenses are not yet in the recipe. The GCP PDS4 labels give the paper DOI as 10.1026/j.icarus.2016.08.012; it is 10.1016/j.icarus.2016.08.012.
entries.revisitWhen: All 18 GCP strips are under source/science/diviner-gcp/ and packages/bake/cli/diviner-gcp-grid.mts has written tbol-noon-compact.tif and tbol-max-compact.tif.
